correctness.rationale: Polarity of the connected unit-edge graph identifies facets with spanning tight-edge potentials. The core K_(p,q) types are (I) zero on A and independent signs on B, and (II) zero on B and independent signs on A; the leaf is tight at both signs. The strictly convex squared centered norm maximizes respectively at q+1-((q+1) mod 2)/N and p+4-(p mod 2)/N, screening leaf-return patterns of norm <=p. Their difference crosses zero exactly at q=p+3. Opposite maximal normals force the center into their common kernel; every other inequality has strict slack locally, so its affine dimension is the computed contact-normal codimension. Integer sign counts are disjoint at p>=5. Independent exact rational sign enumeration checked (p,q)=(5,8),(6,9),(5,3),(6,4), reproducing the threshold, contact multiplicities and contact-normal ranks: 262/0,262/1,10/3,10/5 respectively. These examples corroborate the unbounded algebraic proof, not replace it.
residual_risks: Checks do not enumerate all p,q; reliance on correct tight-graph facet-type classification and treatment of common sign duplicates.
